title: Brownian Motion
description: Interactive simulation demonstrating Brownian motion - the random movement of gas molecules within a confined chamber. Features controls for temperature, molecule count, and chamber size with real-time collision tracking.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Physics
Chemistry
Brownian Motion
Kinetic Molecular Theory
Temperature
Elastic Collisions
Gas Laws
learningObjectives: Explain the relationship between the temperature slider and the average speed of the molecules, and connect it to molecular kinetic energy
Predict how the collisions-per-second display changes when the molecule count is raised from 10 to 100 at a fixed temperature
Describe how shrinking the chamber size increases collision frequency, and relate that result to Boyle's Law and gas pressure
Explain why elastic wall and molecule collisions conserve kinetic energy so the simulation never runs down
Distinguish the random, unpredictable path of an individual molecule from the reproducible macroscopic averages of pressure and temperature
